#### MATERIAL — F1

> Any role the mapping does not name inherits the analysis (weakest) set and the condition is logged — the weaker-profile-is-the-default doctrine.
- **Question**: What identifies "the role" at a spawn for the D7 allowlist mapping? The only per-spawn identity today is RunAgentOptions.label, and it is decorated: pooled fixers run as `fixer-w<n>` and `fixer-w<n>-retry`, batch fixers as `fixer-batch-<cluster.id>`, inspectors as `inspector-w<n>` / `inspector-aggregated`. If the mapping keys on the label string (the design names no other key and adds no role field), every pooled and batched fixer is "unnamed" and inherits the analysis set — no Edit, no Bash — so on the claude route batchVerify and poolSize>1 runs compose fixers that cannot fix, discovered only at runtime. The design must state the key (a new additive role identifier on RunAgentOptions, or documented prefix matching) so `fixer*` variants map to the fixer set.
- **Code evidence**: review-loop/src/issue-processor-attempts.ts:104 label is `fixer${workerSuffix}${attempt > 1 ? `-retry` : ''}`; issue-processor-batch.ts:118 label is `fixer-batch-${cluster.id}`; issue-inspector.ts:107 `inspector${labelSuffix}` and :228 `inspector-aggregated`; review-round.ts:112 `label: 'reviewer'`; issue-matcher.ts:78 `label: 'matcher'`. RunAgentOptions (agent-runner.ts:77-116) carries no role field other than label/slotKey; D2 adds only `backend?`.
- **Resolution**: edited — design.md D7 now states the mapping key: a documented prefix match on RunAgentOptions.label, with the codebase's full label inventory cited (reviewer, matcher, inspector/-w<n>/-aggregated, fixer-w<n>[-retry], fixer-batch-<cluster.id>). fixer* maps to the fixer set, reviewer*/matcher*/inspector* to the analysis set, and any unrecognized label falls to the weakest set — so pooled (poolSize>1) and batched (batchVerify) fixers keep Edit/Bash. Prefix matching over a new role field: no call-site changes, and it rides the same weakest-default guard.

#### NITPICK — F6

> `runAgent` picks the claude decoder when `backend === 'claude'`.
- **Question**: The decoder is selected in `runAgent`, which spans both attempts of the retry-once policy, but `resultOutcome()` is state that must reset per attempt: a first attempt that emitted a result line before stalling would leave `seen: true`, and the retry's exit-0 missing-result check would pass on stale state. `runAttempt` already re-arms `handler.ctx.sessionId` per attempt; the design should state the decoder (and any tool-name correlation state, F5) is created or re-armed per attempt too.
- **Code evidence**: agent-runner.ts:186-191 runAttempt resets `handler.ctx.sessionId = null` and re-spawns per attempt; runAgent (agent-runner.ts:235-256) builds the handler once and runs runAttempt twice on stall/noRetry=false — the same lifetime hazard for any stateful decoder created alongside it.
- **Resolution**: edited — design.md D6 now states the decoder — resultOutcome() and the tool-pairing map — is created per attempt, re-armed in runAttempt beside handler.ctx.sessionId (agent-runner.ts:190 resets it per attempt today), so a retry after a stalled first attempt never reads the stalled attempt's result line as its own.

### Round 8

**Verdict**: 0b 1m 3n · 4 resolved · 0 dismissed · open

#### MATERIAL — F1

> A new `src/claude-stream.ts` exports a decoder factory with the opencode pair's shape: `parseLine(line): OpencodeEvent | null`, `sessionIdOf(line)`, plus `resultOutcome(): { seen: boolean; isError: boolean }`.
- **Question**: D6's own mapping contradicts the decoder interface it pins: the mapping promises "`assistant` content blocks → `tool_use` per tool_use block (`callId` = block id, `input` passthrough for the live arg line, status `running`)" and "`user` tool_result blocks → `tool_use` status `completed` / `error`, paired to the earlier assistant `tool_use` block by `tool_use_id`", but `parseLine(line): OpencodeEvent | null` returns at most ONE event per line. A claude `assistant` line is a whole message whose `content` array can carry multiple `tool_use` blocks (parallel tool calls — the normal shape for a reviewer opening several files), and a `user` line can carry multiple `tool_result` blocks. Implemented as stated, a second tool call in one line is unexpressible: it never enters `seenCalls` (toolCount undercounts), never renders a live arg line, and its later `tool_result` arrives with a `tool_use_id` that has no paired assistant block — which D6 explicitly skips ("A `tool_result` with no paired assistant block is skipped") — so its completion/error status is silently dropped. The specced decode tests cannot catch this: run over the recorded corpus they pass either way, because every corpus assistant line carries at most one tool_use block. The interface needs to return a list (e.g. `parseLine(line): OpencodeEvent[]`, with the opencode default wrapping its single part) or otherwise state how one line yields many events, and the decode tests need a synthetic multi-block line (or a corpus leg) so the per-block behavior is pinned rather than left to the implementer. Which shape does the design intend, and where is the multi-block case exercised?
- **Code evidence**: Answered from the repo. (1) The single-event shape is correct only for opencode: review-loop/src/event-stream.ts parses one `part` per line (parseEventLine reads `raw.part`), so `parseEventLine(line): OpencodeEvent | null` is exact there. (2) The claude corpus confirms one-message-per-line with content arrays: tests/opencode-agent/fixtures/claude-cli/success-turn.ndjson line 3 is an assistant message with content [text, tool_use] and line 4 a user message with one tool_result; adversarial-plan-bash-refused.ndjson has the same shape. A block census over all six .ndjson fixtures shows at most one tool_use per assistant line and one tool_result per user line — so the specced corpus-based decode tests provably cannot exercise the multi-block case. (3) The parent workspace never maps per-block either: opencode-agent/src/claude-contract.ts reduces an assistant line to ONE summary value ({kind:'assistant', tools: string[]} from all blocks, claude-contract.ts:139-143) and a user line to one {kind:'tool-results', succeeded, failed} (:145-150) — the parent's progress layer has no per-call events, so the loop's per-block mapping is new surface with no mirrored doctrine to inherit the interface from. (4) The stream_event line pattern (one content_block_start per block, repeated per tool call in the corpus) corroborates that the CLI emits N blocks per message when N tools are called. (5) No previously resolved finding addresses the return shape: F5 (pairing mechanics), round-5 F2 (text-block drop) and F6 (per-attempt re-arm) all presuppose per-block events work but never reconcile them with the single-event signature.
- **Resolution**: edited — Design D6 corrected to a list-valued decoder: `parseLine(line): OpencodeEvent[]` (was `OpencodeEvent | null`), stating the load-bearing reason — a claude assistant line is one message whose content array can carry several tool_use blocks (parallel tool calls) and a user line several tool_result blocks, and the mapping is per block; a single-event signature would leave a second tool call in one line unexpressible (never in seenCalls, never rendered, its tool_result skipped as unpaired). The opencode-side default is now an adapter wrapping `parseEventLine`'s `OpencodeEvent | null` in a zero-or-one-element array (matching event-stream.ts:96, which parses one `part` per line), `createLineHandler`'s option is restated as 'defaulting to the opencode adapter', and the 'unrecognized line returns `null`' sentence became 'returns an empty list'. Migration step 1's `claude-stream` leg gains a synthetic multi-block fixture leg (one assistant line with two tool_use blocks, one user line with two tool_result blocks, asserting both calls counted/rendered and both results paired) with the census rationale recorded: re-verified against the corpus, every assistant line carries at most one tool_use content block — the second `"tool_use"` string in each fixture line is a `stop_reason` value — so the corpus alone cannot pin the per-block mapping.
